children: Shares of Kalyan Jewellers India rose 3.3 percent to Rs 661 in morning trade on Friday, November 27, after HSBC said jewellery demand remained strong despite a high base. The brokerage also cited the growth potential of the retailer’s affordable gold jewellery brand, Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM).

Kalyan Jewellers was among the top midcap gainers, with a market capitalisation of about Rs 68,300 crore. The stock has gained 36.9 percent so far this year, while the benchmark Nifty 50 has declined 1.2 percent.

HSBC has a Buy rating on Kalyan Jewellers and a target price of Rs 830 per share, implying about 30 percent upside from Thursday’s close. The brokerage highlighted ATM’s competitive making charges and said strong execution at the brand could lift earnings above its current estimates, which exclude ATM’s contribution.

The stock also rallied earlier this week, after Moneycontrol reported that Kalyan Jewellers was in talks with several private equity firms, including former investor Warburg Pincus, to raise close to Rs 2,000 crore through minority stake sales in its subsidiaries Candere and ATM.

A deal with Warburg Pincus would bring the private equity firm back into the Kalyan group more than two years after it completed its exit from the listed retailer in August 2024. Warburg Pincus invested about Rs 1,700 crore in two rounds between 2014 and 2017, helping Kalyan Jewellers expand from its South Indian base into northern and western India as well as overseas markets.

Kalyan Jewellers reported a 63.6 percent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 427 crore for the September quarter, from Rs 260.51 crore a year earlier. The quarter included a Rs 73 crore exceptional gain from the sale of a non-core land parcel. Excluding that gain, net profit rose nearly 36 percent to about Rs 354 crore.

Consolidated revenue rose 31.4 percent to Rs 10,323 crore from Rs 7,856 crore a year earlier, crossing the Rs 10,000 crore mark. Following the results, UBS maintained its Buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 900 per share.

title: Kalyan Jewellers stock jumps over 3%; HSBC bullish on demand, growth potential of affordable gold brand
